amendments.rule: A vocative noun takes a supplied *O*, *ye*, or *thou* into its own unit, never `added`. **An article on the vocative does not take that pronoun.** The article takes only what the ASV actually writes for it, which for a vocative is usually nothing: `הַכֹּהֲנִים` → *ye priests* and `הַזְּקֵנִים` → *ye old men* are an `unrepresented` article beside a noun holding the whole *ye priests*, exactly as the far commoner anarthrous vocative is handled, and `הַמֶּלֶךְ` → *O king* goes the same way. Where the ASV instead builds a relative around the vocative — `הַחֲרֵדִים` → *ye that tremble* — the article takes the *that* under rule 41, and the *ye* still stays with the noun. Rule 41's supplied pronoun is the substantival article's; the vocative *ye* is not, since the anarthrous vocative supplies it with no article present at all. **But an imperative standing in the same clause has its own claim on such a pronoun, and the ASV's word order is what allocates it.** English writes an imperative's subject pronoun immediately after the verb and a vocative's immediately before the noun, so where a verb and a vocative both stand in the clause and the ASV writes a single *ye* or *thou*, read which word it stands beside: a pronoun written after the imperative is that verb's subject pronoun under rule 17, and one written before the vocative noun is the noun's under this rule. `הַלְלוּהוּ שֶׁמֶשׁ וְיָרֵחַ` → *Praise* ***ye*** *him, sun and moon* gives the *ye* to the verb and leaves the vocative its bare *sun*, while `הַלְלוּהוּ כָּל־כּוֹכְבֵי אוֹר` → *Praise him, all* ***ye*** *stars of light* gives it to `כּוֹכָב` and leaves the imperative its bare *Praise*; one verse may write both shapes, as PSA.148.3 does. Count the ASV's pronouns against the morphemes that could carry them, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s: where the ASV writes one for each — *Praise ye him, ye heavens* — each morpheme takes the one standing beside its own word, and where it writes none at all neither takes anything, the verb keeping only its own word under rule 17 and the vocative under this rule's first sentence. Position is what decides this and nothing else, because the two readings differ in no other respect: rule 14 reads a `וְעַתָּה` pair by which morpheme's own lexeme each English word writes, and rule 51 disregards a postposed *also*'s distance from the waw that licenses it, but a supplied subject pronoun writes no lexeme at all and both morphemes license it, so adjacency is the only evidence there is. An *O* the ASV writes before the vocative is that noun's on the same terms and is never the imperative's, since English writes no *O* for a verb's subject.
amendments.why: PSA.148 aligns eleven imperative-plus-vocative colons in which the ASV writes a single supplied pronoun, and rules 17 and 36 each license that word without saying which morpheme takes it when both stand in the clause. The chapter settled it by adjacency and applied that uniformly, including PSA.148.3, which writes both shapes in one verse: *Praise ye him, sun and moon* gives the pronoun to the verb, and *Praise him, all ye stars of light* gives it to the noun. The corpus corroborates both sides and contradicts neither — `הָלַל` is aligned to *praise ye* headed on *praise* in nine units, and `שָׁמַיִם` to *ye heavens* and *O ye heavens* in three, with `אֶרֶץ` → *O earth* in five more. Written as an amendment rather than a new rule so that rule 36's own text carries the qualification, and worded to cover *thou* and *O* as well as *ye*, since the same allocation arises for each.

conventions: An English coordinator written between two juxtaposed phrases goes to a preposition standing where the connective stands only where that preposition's own sense is what the coordinator states. The comitative preposition of `זְקֵנִים עִם־נְעָרִים` → *Old men* ***and*** *children* takes the written *and* under rule 11, since dropping the word leaves that preposition's relation unstated and nothing else diminished. The second `לְ` of `לָעַד לְעוֹלָם` → *for ever* ***and*** *ever* takes nothing and is `unrepresented` under rule 40 while the *and* is `added` under rule 14, since *and* states nothing of that preposition's duration relation; this is rule 14's own reading of `לְיוֹשְׁבֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם אֶל־אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל` → *concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem* ***and*** *the land of Israel*, where a second prepositional phrase with its own written preposition is juxtaposed and the supplied coordinator is still `added`. Rule 26's `בֵּין X לְ Y` and `מִן … עַד` carve-outs were considered for PSA.148.6 and set aside as naming their own constructions. BSB represents that `לְ` and this chapter does not; that is the documented convention difference and not a correction.

report: All ten candidate lemma groups were read against the verses. Every multi-treatment bucket is accounted for by what the ASV printed, not by one construction analysed two ways, so no patch is owed.

Supplied *ye* is the group that looks like a split and is not. The chapter allocates each single written pronoun by adjacency: after the imperative it is that verb's subject pronoun under rule 17 (PSA.148.1 s001/s003, PSA.148.2 s001/s006, PSA.148.3 s001, PSA.148.14 s018), before the vocative noun it is the noun's under rule 36 (PSA.148.3 s009 'ye stars', PSA.148.4 s003/s008, PSA.148.7 s007). PSA.148.3 writes both shapes in one verse and the chapter used the one test on both. Neither rule 17 nor rule 36 says how to allocate the word when a verb and a vocative both stand in the colon and only one pronoun is written, so that gap is amended into rule 36.

Coordinators are the folded-versus-added kind of split the lemma table is blind to, so the dump was read end to end for them. The chapter holds exactly two supplied connectives: the 'and' of LA-AD LE-OLAM -> 'for ever and ever' (PSA.148.6), marked added with the second lamed unrepresented, and the 'and' of ZEQENIM IM-NEARIM -> 'Old men and children' (PSA.148.12), given to the comitative IM under rule 11. The difference is source-licensed: 'and' states the very relation IM bears and states nothing of the lamed's duration relation, and PSA.148.6 is rule 14's own EL-ADMAT YISRAEL reading. Recorded as a convention, since a reader working from rule 14's closing sentences alone would mark the IM case added.

Remaining groups check out. The waw is rendered 'also' (PSA.148.6, rule 51), 'And' (PSA.148.14), 'which' (PSA.148.6, rule 17's relative recasting) and 'and' elsewhere, each the word the ASV wrote. Every unrepresented article is one for which the ASV writes no determiner at all (PSA.148.4 s004 and s007, PSA.148.9 s001, PSA.148.10 s001), and every written 'the' went to the morpheme it stands before, which is why ERETS and SHAMAYIM are read one way as a rectum with a supplied determiner (PSA.148.11) and another as a bare noun with one (PSA.148.13).

BSB: five disagreements, none a genuine error. The four Td cases (PSA.148.4, .9, .10) are vocative and rectum articles for which the ASV writes no 'the' at all, so rules 29 and 36 leave them unrepresented; the PSA.148.6 lamed is the documented BSB convention of attaching a preposition to its phrase, and the ASV leaves that preposition's own relation unstated.

Reviewed and left standing: PSA.148.13 unit 9, the three-morpheme LEVADDO -> 'alone', a single occurrence whose note already names the competing split under rule 22; and PSA.148.14's added 'Even', which stands before a phrase whose lamed already holds its own 'of' and which no marker reaches.
